task: This is a synthetic writing exercise. Using these fictional reporting notes, write a newspaper reported feature for general readers. Draw only on the supplied notes; do not invent additional reported events, scenes, or quotations. Write from this reporting snapshot as of August 12, 2025. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: The Coastal Mangrove Carbon Alliance issued 1.8 million carbon credits between 2018 and 2024, representing claimed carbon sequestration in Tambela Province mangrove forests; a VCMIO audit found the forests claimed as protected had already been legally protected under national conservation law since 2011.
The 1.8 million credits were sold at prices ranging from $18 to $45 per credit, generating an estimated $54 million in revenue.
Lighthouse Shipping Group, a maritime company, purchased 420,000 of those credits to support its 2022 and 2023 carbon neutrality claims.
Lighthouse sustainability director Marcus Ferreira said the company conducted due diligence through its certification vendor and was not told about the legal protection status of the mangroves.

Ferreira said: "We paid for verified carbon reduction. We now know the verification was inadequate. We're responsible for the money we spent. We are not responsible for a fraud we had no way to detect."

An investigative journalism team that reviewed Lighthouse's original due diligence records found no evidence the company asked whether the forests were independently protected before being enrolled in the program.
Coastal Mangrove Carbon Alliance's founder, fictionally named Paulo Avila, has not responded to media inquiries since the audit was released; his company's website went offline in July 2025.

Carbon market transparency advocate Dr. Ruth Nkosi of International Carbon Accountability Center said: "The buyers' defense is 'we were defrauded.' But due diligence in this market has been aspirational, not operational. Most buyers never asked the hard questions."

Lighthouse has committed to purchasing replacement credits from a VCMIO-verified program and to not counting the disputed credits toward its emissions claims; it has not disclosed whether it will seek legal recourse.
Four other companies that purchased Coastal Mangrove Alliance credits have disputed the VCMIO's finding; two have hired independent auditors to review their specific purchases.
The VCMIO said buyers who can demonstrate good faith due diligence may receive a grace period to replace disputed credits; the standard for good faith has not yet been published.
Dr. Nkosi said the Coastal Mangrove case illustrates a structural problem: the entities being paid to certify credits have a financial relationship with the sellers, not the buyers.
Ferreira said Lighthouse began internally reviewing all its credit purchases in July 2025 and will not purchase new voluntary credits until the review is complete.
At least six similar mangrove and forest protection programs in Tambela Province are being examined by the VCMIO; Avila's program was the largest.

Dr. Nkosi said the underlying science of mangrove carbon sequestration is sound; the fraud was in the additionality claim — the assertion that the protection was newly provided — not in the fact that mangroves store carbon.
Lighthouse's 2022 annual report included a graphic labeling the company as 'carbon neutral'; the company has removed that designation from its website pending the credit review.
Securities analysts said the reputational risk to companies that prominently marketed carbon neutrality claims based on disputed credits may exceed the financial cost of replacing the credits.
Ferreira declined to quantify the potential cost of replacing the 420,000 disputed credits at current market prices.

The VCMIO said it will publish new mandatory additionality standards in early 2026 that will require program developers to demonstrate protection additionality against a documented counterfactual, not just a claim.
Dr. Nkosi said the voluntary carbon market has a credibility problem that is now visible to its customers: "The question is whether the response is serious reform or the appearance of it."

forbidden_additions: a criminal charge against Avila or the Alliance
a claim that Lighthouse knowingly purchased fraudulent credits
a revenue figure different from $54 million
